_comment: Figures no API can supply: money awarded, people mentored, talks given, reviews done.
These used to live in a `static` block inside data/stats.json, which made that file
half script-written and half yours — the one place the 'never edit generated files'
rule needed an exception. Splitting them out removes the exception: stats.json is now
entirely machine-written, and this file is entirely yours.
Read by scripts/emit-metrics-tex.js (into CV macros), js/modules/stats.js (the website's
Stats cards), and citable from an application as `service:<key>`.
Update these by hand when the numbers change. Nothing will do it for you.
_comment_proposals: Proposals WRITTEN, not proposals funded. `fundingAwarded` above is the funded total and
covers exactly one award (data/awards.json fcs-2025). Keeping the two apart is the point:
'led 8 proposals' and 'one is funded' are different claims and a cover letter must not let
_comment_talks: `invitedTalks` is a CAREER total and includes talks given before joining Woodwell in Jan
2022. A promotion or performance case needs the since-2022 subset, and there is no year
data here to derive it from.
There is deliberately NO `invitedTalksSince2022` key yet. Adding it as null would be worse
than absent: verify-application.js treats a resolved-but-null value as a valid citation
(it tests for undefined), so a claim could cite an uncounted figure and still pass. Absent,
the same citation fails loudly. Add the key when the talks are actually counted.
